LESSON: MANAGEMENT OF SOLID WASTE

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter 2.1 Properties of Matter (14 lessons) ● Meaning of matter ● States of mat
Topic 2.2: Management of Solid Waste
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Management of Solid Waste, part of Matter 2.1 Properties of Matter (14 lessons) ● Meaning of matter ● States of mat in Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How is solid waste dangerous to the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. walk around the school compound and its environment to identify solid waste in the environment,

2. discuss with peers the meaning of decomposable and non-decomposable solid waste,

3. collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing,

4. discuss the dangers of solid waste to the environment and present in class,

5. discuss methods of managing different types of waste in their environment (To include Re-using, Recycling and Reducing), Hint: Include common waste in school and environment such as kitchen, animal waste, plastics, e-waste, metals and glasses,

6. practice observe proper safety measures in solid waste

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. walk around the school compound and its environment to identify solid waste in the environment,
2. discuss with peers the meaning of decomposable and non-decomposable solid waste,
3. collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing,
4. discuss the dangers of solid waste to the environment and present in class,
5. discuss methods of managing different types of waste in their environment (To include Re-using, Recycling and Reducing), Hint: Include common waste in school and environment such as kitchen, animal waste, plastics, e-waste, metals and glasses,
6. practice observe proper safety measures in solid waste

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Management of Solid Waste together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner reflects and practices good ways of managing different types of waste in their

environment as they collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing.

● Learning to learn: The learner explores ways of making dustbins, toys or ornaments from locally available materials

Values:
Responsibility: The learner plays different roles from other peers as they use locally available materials to make dustbins, toys

and ornaments.

Patriotism: The learner practices carrying out community service activities as they collect solid waste in the school, sort and

classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Health issues: The learner learns about preventive health measures as they discuss the dangers of solid waste to the environment

and presents in class.

• Socio-economic issues; environmental education: The learner discusses ways of managing different types of solid waste in their

environment and generate outcome out of the locally available waste by making dustbins, toys and ornaments.

Link to Other Learning Area:

Creative arts: The learner uses knowledge on management of solid waste to make ornaments and dustbins.
